_help: Day 3, room 6: the shed, 'The girl at the flower stall' (1955-1957). The market picture's tiles; the sunflower Saturdays and the wedding day (Day 2's note) for the bicycle lock; Maman's weights riddle for the workbench drawer. See docs/STORY.md.

locks._why: The side door key was in the workbench drawer.
hints: The side way round is locked.
The shell key from the workbench drawer opens the side door.
Select the shell key, then tap the side door.

locks._why: The market picture's tiles are turned; put the picture right.
hints: Some of the picture on the wall is upside down.
Tap the tiles of the turned-up picture to turn them.
Line up the awning and the flowers: every tile must match its neighbours.

locks._why: One sunflower every Saturday for a year (52), then the day in June she married him: the 18th, from the wedding note of the second day. 52, then 18.
hints: How many Saturdays in a year? And which day in June mattered most?
The price board note belongs to the bicycle; the wedding day is in your notebook, from the second morning.

locks._why: Chloé keeps bumping into things; her brush was in the bicycle basket. Brushed, she drops a memory.
hints: Her fringe is over her eyes: the brush was in the bicycle basket.
Select the brush, then tap Chloé.

locks._why: Maman's weights note slid under the workbench; only Chloé fits.
hints: Tap Chloé, then tap under the workbench.

locks._why: Small + middle + big = 11; middle = small + 1; big = 2 x middle: 2, 3 and 6 kilos, smallest first, at the bench where she counted the money.
hints: Maman's three weights: work them out.
The weights riddle belongs to the workbench's left drawer.
